input_format: raw sequence of HTTP/2 wire frames
configuration_profile: stateful SETTINGS, PING, GOAWAY and WINDOW_UPDATE handlers with fresh nginx pool, minimal HTTP/2 server configuration, one primary stream, a closed indexed node, and a second synthetic waiting stream
allocator_mode: NGX_DEBUG_PALLOC=1 with a fresh nginx pool for each fragmentation replay
justification: NGX-IF11 stops after frame-header dispatch and therefore cannot detect memory-safety or arithmetic defects in control-frame bodies and persistent connection state.
state: Each input is parsed four times with identical bytes: contiguously, byte-by-byte, in three-byte fragments and with an input-selected fragment size. Concatenated frames share settings, flow-control and output-queue state within a replay.
known_limitations: Only SETTINGS, PING, GOAWAY and WINDOW_UPDATE frames are accepted.
Only the primary stream is request-bearing; the second stream exists solely to model WINDOW_UPDATE waiting-queue traversal, while request parsing and the full stream lifecycle are not entered.
Generated ACK/PING frames are allocated and queued but not written to a socket.
The protocol-error teardown guard and synthetic connection driver are applied only to the isolated instrumented build copy.

scopes.contract: Validate SETTINGS framing and values, update connection settings and queue an acknowledgement.
scopes.preconditions: Fresh HTTP/2 connection with default windows/frame size and one minimal live stream.

scopes.contract: Validate eight-byte PING frames and queue echo acknowledgements.
scopes.preconditions: Connection-level stream ID zero for accepted frames.

scopes.contract: Validate GOAWAY minimum length and connection-level stream ID, then skip optional debug data.
scopes.preconditions: At least eight declared payload bytes for an accepted frame.

scopes.contract: Validate flow-control increments and update connection or stream windows, wake waiting/exhausted streams, and ignore unknown streams safely.
scopes.preconditions: Default connection and stream send windows, one live exhausted/waiting stream at ID 1, a closed indexed node at ID 3, a second exhausted/waiting stream, and a callback that can optionally drain the connection window.
variants: stop queue walk when callback drains connection window to zero
